record.paper_title: 20 Open Questions About Deformations of Compactifiable Manifolds
record.context_brief: Infinite deformation families for noncompact Calabi-Yau threefolds
record.original_question: Let X be a noncompact Calabi-Yau threefold. What geometric conditions on X imply that X has infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic deformations?

evidence.quote: Question 18. Let X be a noncompact Calabi–Yau threefold. What geometric conditions on X imply that it has infinitely many nonisomorphic deformations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Calabi–Yau threefold is a smooth complex three-dimensional manifold X with trivial canonical bundle K_X ≅ O_X and (in the noncompact setting) which is not required to be projective or compact. A deformation of X is a flat family π : 𝒳 → B over a connected complex base B with a distinguished point 0 ∈ B such that π^{-1}(0) ≅ X; two deformations are said to give nonisomorphic threefolds if their general fibers are not biholomorphic to each other.

Problem. Identify geometric conditions on a noncompact Calabi–Yau threefold X that guarantee the existence of infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic complex deformations of X. More precisely, find natural hypotheses on X (for example, on its topology, its asymptotic/end structure, the existence and configuration of compact or noncompact divisors and curves, the behavior of its holomorphic volume form, or the dimension of its deformation space H^1(X, T_X)) that imply the set of isomorphism classes of small deformations of X is infinite.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as one of twenty open problems concerning deformations of compactifiable manifolds, and no later work appears to provide a definitive set of geometric conditions characterizing when a noncompact Calabi–Yau threefold admits infinitely many nonisomorphic deformations. The problem appears to remain open.
